study: Bierman et al. 2008 (Head Start REDI, Penn State, Child Development 79(6))
eval_evidence: The authors (Bierman, Domitrovich, Greenberg et al., Penn State) developed REDI (and the embedded Preschool PATHS curriculum) and conducted the evaluation -- developer-conducted.
developer_evidence: Weekly mentoring/coaching was 'provided by local educational consultants (“REDI trainers”), experienced' staff trained for the project -- not the developers/research team themselves.
cascade_evidence: The research team trained local educational consultants ('REDI trainers'), who in turn provided the on-site weekly mentoring/coaching to the teachers (developer -> REDI trainers -> teachers, >=1 extra hop).
counterfactual_evidence: Comparison condition was 'usual practice' Head Start (business-as-usual control).
coaching_evidence: 'Ongoing weekly mentoring support' (~3 hrs/classroom/week) by REDI trainers to support teachers' use of the curricula/strategies in their own classrooms -- recurring weekly in-class coaching.
student_dose_evidence: REDI is a manualized enrichment curriculum (Preschool PATHS lessons, interactive book-reading, Sound Games) 'delivered by classroom teachers and integrated into their ongoing' Head Start day -- teacher-delivered enrichment, not a separate tutoring/pull-out/added-minutes student dose.
maturity_evidence: REDI is a single Head Start (preschool) year enrichment program; outcomes measured at the end of that one program year for teachers new to it -- one-year design, no maturity axis.
